E -Plan The Elevator Lobby was designed with a minimum dimension of 8 feet. However, an additional wood veneer will be added to the walls, creating a minimum dimension of 7’9”. This dimension and veneer addition can be seen in the diagram attached to the bottom of the letter in the electronic plans attachment. According to Section 403.6.1 of 780 CMR 8th Edition, buildings more than 70 feet in height above grade plane must provide a minimum of one fire service access elevator in accordance with Section 3007. Section 3007.4.4 states that the elevator lobby is permitted a minimum dimension of 8 feet. 32 Derne Street is 90 feet in height and therefore must comply with these requirements. The 9th Edition 780 CMR is anticipated to be adopted within the next few months. According to the 9th Edition, and the 2015 IBC, a fire service access elevator is not required unless the building is more than 120 feet in height. The Fifth Floor of 32 Derne Street is new construction and could therefore fall under the 9th Edition. Under the 9th Edition, a fire service access elevator is not required and therefore, the minimum dimension of 7’9” would be permitted. We are requesting to follow the 9th edition for the construction of the Fifth Floor of 32 Derne Street, rather than the 8th edition, as the 9th will soon be adopted.

Adding a canopy to replace awning.
SITE OF WORK The 1 ½ story house is a L -shaped , wood- framed with brick veneer built in 1950. THE OBJECTIVE This work will improve the exterior with no changes to the existing structure. Changes will be made on the inside corner of the “L” within the existing footprint of the dwelling. I will replace the awning over the landing with a wood-framed structure creating a covered entry area approximately 5x5 feet. I will alter the direction of snow accumulation and eliminate ice on the landing while creating a “beefier” canopy. DESIGN The design mimics the-low hip canopy commonly employed in ”L”-shaped houses in the 1950’s. Framing will be covered by ¾ inch stock with decorative elements (transom) expected to improve the appearance of the home in a manner fitting the original design. The basic design is copied from 457 Parker Street in Newton , MA of which 2 photos are provided. STRUCTURE The concrete base, original to the house and is level without signs of settlement. The existing roof structure is framed with 2 X 8s without any observable faults. Photos are provided of the existing site. • A 6 “X 6” Colum will be attached to the base with a Simpson Standoff Bracket or similar. (see Front Sketch ) • The top of the Column will be lagged to a 2” X 6” ceiling frame that will tie to the existing structure with joist hangers. (see Ceiling Sketch). In addition to the 2” X 6” members that rim the “ceiling” a central member will be added to provide additional rigidity. • Rafters framing be 2” X 6” stock. A Ridge Rafter of modest slope will be secured at the existing valley of this L-shaped home. Two 2” X 6” “Plates” will secured to the existing roof to which the 2” X 6” Jacks will be attached. The Jack Rafters will be spaced 16” on center. (see Rafter Sketch). • Each of the longest Jacks will be secured to the 2” X 6 “ joist shown in the ceiling sketch in order to provide stiffening as shown in the Rafter Sketch. FINISHING Flashing and Ice &; Snow membrane will be covered by 3-tab shingles matching the existing surface. Gutters and Downspouts will be attached to the new structure and will terminate in the same place as the current downspout.

AT&;T is proposing to install (12) antennas and an 11.5' x 20' equipment shelter on the rooftop of 250 Cambridge Street (aka 8 Anderson Street). Verizon is currently installed on the rooftop and AT&;T will be mirroring their installation as closely as possible. There are three sectors (Alpha/Beta/Gamma). Each sector will have (4) antennas. The Beta Sector will be mounted to the equipment shelter on the southern portion of the roof. The antennas will be mounted to the end of the shelter then enclosed in stealth walls which will match the shelter, making the antennas invisible from the surrounding properties. The Alpha sector will be mounted on the eastern wall of the existing elevator shaft. They will be facade mounted and the back of the antennas will be 3.5" from the wall itself. The antennas will also be located 1.0' below the top of the elevator shaft roof. These antennas will be painted to match the elevator shaft to which they are attached. The Gamma sector will be located on the northern portion of the rooftop and the antennas will be placed inside of a stealth faux chimney. The antennas will not be visible to the surrounding properties. Final Configuration: (12) antennas, (9) TMAs, (6) Radiohead Units, (3) Surge Arrestors, (3) E911 GPS Antennas and a 11.5' x 20' equipment shelter.
